oracle_checkpoints: Capture state before/after90B651, after8B0630, after905000, after90B750, and after90B270; distinguish partially published object from returned success.
Keep original name, normalized cache name, .ini path, INI shared result, fallback temporary and parent pointers separately identifiable across callbacks and recursive requests.
Require actual source-selected file bytes/import results; stop before unsupported RemoveDirectoryA, file mutation, CRT, type-decoder or callback behavior.
Observe real short/long names, base/nonzero skins and formatting boundaries without replacing CRT formatting or INI values.
Track exact allocations and lifetimes for provider map/name, borrowed directory, cache keys, manager index aliases, active-entry callable storage and INI-manager file pairs.
For recursion or callback-mutated state, preserve native rereads and record an explicit boundary/fault; never treat a cycle, null allocation or unsupported callback as success.
Capture destruction order plus each physical free; distinguish normal source return, abandoned probe storage and unimplemented SEH/OOM recovery.
Run future probes in a fresh machine state with actual CRT initialization and declared confined filesystem profile; no requalification of the earlier null-context/failed exploratory fixtures.
